title: E1 Governance schemas and shared security invariants
description: Define tenant/principal/policy/key versions, control-plane RBAC versus data-plane entitlements, a single deny-by-default evaluator shared by model listing and inference, capability manifest, audit envelope, and cache-version contracts.

title: E2 Distributed virtual-key lifecycle
description: Harden existing OSS key CRUD with reveal-once hashed secrets, status/expiry/not-before, transactional rotation/revocation, versioned cross-pod invalidation, bounded stale-cache fail-closed behavior, audited bulk operations, and three-pod tests.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: 2026-07-16 VK image-hotpath audit found and fixed a real bypass: the three-pod oracle previously inspected cache state but never authenticated created/rotated/deleted secrets, allowing /v1/models to return 200 for a rotated secret. The handler now resolves supplied VKs from the governance pod-local authority cache, rejects missing/inactive/revoked keys with 401, and honors the bounded freshness lease with 503 instead of doing a per-request DB lookup. The strengthened k3s/local-Aurora oracle now proves create accepted on all 3 pods, old secret rejected after rotate, new secret accepted, deleted secret rejected, restart replay, and inference+MCP stale-close after Postgres partition. Full loose-binary 3-node run passed. Next required proof is the same oracle against the immutable published v0.3.4 image digest.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: 2026-07-16 strengthened serving-path audit exposed a second, broader VK bypass: on ordinary /v1/chat/completions, provider queue lookup ran before GovernancePlugin.PreLLMHook, so an old rotated secret reached provider discovery and returned 400 provider-not-configured instead of the authority 401. Strict TDD reproduced the ordering defect for both non-streaming and streaming requests. Commit bd593033f moves provider discovery after plugin short-circuit and post-routing identity in both paths. Full core tests, targeted race tests, vet, and the local three-node oracle passed; the oracle now proves rotated/deleted rejection on both list-models and chat plus list-models/chat/MCP stale-close after the PostgreSQL authority partition. Immutable released-image proof remains required before closing.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: 2026-07-16: API audit found rotation already implemented at POST /api/governance/virtual-keys/{vk_id}/rotate with row-lock/CAS, durable invalidation, reload, and one-time secret response. Added GET /api/governance/virtual-keys/{vk_id}/reveal (no-store, redacted metadata plus secret) and UI client typing in commit 6a3513b8d. Recommended identity model: one durable user VK across workstations for shared authorization/budget, with separate short-lived session/device IDs for audit and targeted revocation; Okta/SCIM should map principal to the durable VK, not mint per-device budget identities.

title: Prove cross-pod key coherence and bounded revocation
description: Implement versioned invalidation consumption and cache freshness leases. Test a key created on pod A across all pods, duplicate/reordered events, disconnection, revocation under load, emergency rotation and fail-closed behavior after the staleness SLO.
notes:
Foreground VK slice includes af9bc6fbb (transactional durable outbox, ordered per-pod consumer, freshness lease/fail-closed governance, create/rotate/delete producers, team/customer propagation) and 0f5cb1894 (reproducible three-pod k3d/PostgreSQL create on A, rotate on B, delete on C, exact monotonic outbox, replacement-pod replay without resurrection under an in-cluster 8-second oracle). MCP authority work adds e175d2600 and 38a982647 for cross-pod MCP control records, runtime convergence, disabled-grant denial, generation-serialized retries, and transactional VK credential reconciliation. Commit 6f2156337 now makes MCP-originated config, assignment, OAuth/header credential, schema, and outbox mutations atomic; serializes credential callbacks and MCP/VK assignment writers with MCP-to-VK-to-assignment lock order; rejects stale PATCH snapshots with 409; and removes compensating DB rollback after runtime failure. Verified by full configstore, race, and full HTTP handler suites plus real PostgreSQL tests for a first-credential callback versus revocation, MCP-side versus VK-side assignment replacement, and crossed two-MCP/two-VK historical-holder lock sets. Independent final review found no release blocker in this slice. Remains open because bif-kyy.3.2 is unresolved and revocation-under-load, DB-disconnect process-level 503, emergency-overlap rotation, full mixed-version binary, and multi-node/Aurora matrices remain unproven.

Commit dea24cf49 adds optional PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY wake hints over the durable VK outbox without making notifications authoritative: dedicated pgx session outside the GORM pool, constant transaction-coalesced payload, reconnect jitter/backoff through accept-then-drop flaps, PasswordCommand refresh, listener cancellation, mandatory periodic fallback, and wake-storm suppression during DB failures. Verification: full framework/configstore and HTTP server suites; focused race suites; real k3s PostgreSQL commit-versus-rollback delivery and one-connection pool isolation; independent blocker review; and a freshly rebuilt three-pod create-on-A/rotate-on-B/delete-on-C/replacement replay oracle with exact reload,reload,delete outbox ordering. The k3s harness now forces binary-digest rollouts and recreates its explicitly test-only public schema each run to prevent stale-binary and encryption-state false results. Remains open for revocation-under-load, DB-disconnect process-level fail-closed recovery, emergency-overlap rotation, mixed-version, multi-node, and real Aurora/RDS Proxy matrices.

Benchmark multi-pod concurrency, lock wait, deadlocks, WAL/I/O and hot-tenant behavior; retain only the simplest design meeting launch throughput.

title: Implement controlled overdraft approval, policy and alerting workflow
description: Overdraft is allowed only by a preconfigured user/team rule or explicit approval. Define amount/time/model scope, approver RBAC, expiry, idempotency and audit. Alert affected user and operators at warning, breach, approval, consumption and expiry through configurable in-product plus webhook/email channels. Emergency top-up must propagate within 1-5 seconds.

title: Bound stream accumulation, capture fanout and cancellation cleanup
description: Introduce purpose-specific byte/time budgets, rolling digests or encrypted spill, metadata-only downgrade and retained-byte metrics. Prove disabled capture creates no durable raw copy and soak without OOM.
notes: Third TDD review-fix slice completed for release-blocking stream retention defects, scoped to framework/streaming and framework/tracing. Implemented: (1) NewAccumulator now uses conservative nonzero production retention defaults for output/raw/passthrough/header capture, while NewAccumulatorWithOptions preserves explicit zero/unlimited compatibility; NewTracer inherits these defaults and exposes accumulator options for verification. (2) Raw response capture no longer fmt.Sprintf-expands []byte/json.RawMessage before limit decisions; it streams through a type-aware bounded writer with exact byte counts and SHA-256 digests for string, []byte, and json.RawMessage. (3) Tracer registers a cancellation watcher so a canceled streaming context force-cleans the accumulator even if no later chunk arrives. (4) Metadata-only/drop mode now keeps bounded de-dupe sets across chat/text, responses, audio, transcription, image, and raw accounting, so duplicate plugin deliveries do not double-count after downgrade. (5) Passthrough headers now have count, name-byte, value-byte, and aggregate-byte caps with capture metadata. (6) Passthrough final raw capture is applied before the Capture snapshot. (7) Retained chunks are returned to pools on downgrade and rejected/duplicate/early-error chunks are reset immediately; pooldebug-tag tests pass. Added regression coverage for constructor defaults, exact raw bytes/digest/accounting, no-later-chunk cancellation cleanup, post-downgrade duplicate deliveries across modalities/raw, passthrough header flooding, final raw snapshot ordering, and rejected chunk pool return. Verified: gofmt; cd framework && go test -count=1 ./streaming ./tracing PASS; cd framework && go test -race -count=1 ./streaming ./tracing PASS; cd framework && go vet ./streaming ./tracing PASS; cd framework && go test -tags pooldebug -count=1 ./streaming ./tracing PASS; git diff --check PASS. Bead remains open: encrypted spill is still unimplemented and only in-repo bounded soak evidence exists, not a prolonged production-scale soak/OOM run.

title: Refactor MCP invocation so mandatory policy precedes credential and connection acquisition
description: Resolve immutable tool/client manifest without credentials, run mandatory parameter/approval policy, then issue attenuated credential and acquire connection. Finalize denied/preparation-failed/ambiguous executions into evidence receipts. Replace permissive eager injection with authorized signed catalog snapshots.
acceptance_criteria:
Done when:
- MCP execution order is normalize immutable target, mandatory policy, attenuated credential, connection, wire call and terminal receipt.
- Unit and sequence-conformance tests prove denied calls issue zero credentials, acquire zero connections and send zero upstream packets.
- Integration tests finalize policy denial, preparation failure, timeout and ambiguous completion into distinct evidence states.
- Authorized catalog snapshots replace permissive eager/server-wide grants and bind exact tool/schema digests.
- Mock-free MCP E2E covers alias collision, stale tool, injected arguments/results, pod loss and reconnect.
- Rollback feature flag restores the prior execution path only in environments where mandatory MCP invocation is disabled.

title: Implement Flywheel specification-derived conformance harness
description: Enumerate EV-MUST/SHOULD requirements from the evaluation conformance spec, attach stable IDs to executable tests, generate COVERAGE and compliance JSON/Markdown, track intentional deviations as XFAIL with owner/review date, and refuse conformance with any untested MUST.
acceptance_criteria:
Done when:
- COVERAGE maps every EV-MUST and EV-SHOULD ID to an executable test and source requirement.
- All 20 MUST requirements have 100% tested coverage; no MUST may be SKIP.
- Known divergences use XFAIL with owner, rationale, affected cases and review date in DISCREPANCIES.md.
- Conformance runner emits deterministic compliance JSON and Markdown with passing, failing, XFAIL and untested counts.
- CI regression tests prove a deliberately removed MUST test makes the harness report non-conformant.
notes: Launch scope is the canonical contract/privacy/MR authorization subset described in docs/roadmap/jsm-flywheel-evaluation-conformance-spec.md; the full Flywheel matrix is a maturity target.

title: Implement provenance-backed Flywheel golden artifact suite
description: Canonicalize and freeze reviewed skill contracts, envelopes, scorecards, promotion/rollback receipts and dependency graphs. Record generator/source/privacy/reviewer provenance; forbid CI auto-update; emit reviewable diffs and split artifacts over 100 KB.
acceptance_criteria:
Done when:
- Canonical goldens cover contracts, envelopes, scorecards, promotion/rollback receipts and dependency graphs.
- Every fixture records generator command, source revision, dependency lock, privacy class and human reviewer in PROVENANCE.md.
- Unit and snapshot tests scrub only approved dynamic fields and preserve security-relevant differences.
- CI cannot update goldens and uploads .actual plus unified diffs on mismatch.
- Review tooling rejects artifacts over 100KB unless decomposed or explicitly approved with rationale.
notes: Deferred from the internal-marketplace launch path. Reconsider if autonomous merging, external publishers, offline distribution, employee analytics, or evidence-based production selection is introduced.

title: Implement Flywheel metamorphic and mutation-testing suite
description: Implement only scored MRs at or above 2.0 using property-based generation, including ID rename, reorder, dedup, privacy loss, permission change, evaluator change, deletion and rollback graph relations. Plant the documented mutations and require at least 80 percent kill rate or justified equivalent/unreachable classification.
acceptance_criteria:
Done when:
- All implemented metamorphic relations have strength score >= 2.0 and property-based generators.
- Suite includes ID rename, reorder, dedup, privacy loss, permission change, evaluator change, deletion and rollback graph relations.
- Every relation kills at least one documented planted mutation.
- Aggregate mutation kill rate is >= 80%, with every survivor classified as killed, equivalent, unreachable or coverage gap.
- Compound rename-reorder-dedup and privacy-loss-pod-count-replay relations run deterministically in CI.
notes: Deferred from the internal-marketplace launch path. Reconsider if autonomous merging, external publishers, offline distribution, employee analytics, or evidence-based production selection is introduced.

title: Implement structure-aware fuzz and real-service Flywheel E2E campaigns
description: Add narrow Go fuzz targets for envelopes, contracts, reducers, state machines, graphs, privacy, outbox, MCP, pools and assignment; enforce throughput/corpus/triage gates. Add real PostgreSQL and multi-process E2E for outage isolation, loss, convergence, deletion, recall, MCP ordering, privacy canaries, evaluator separation, differencing and mixed versions.
acceptance_criteria:

- Narrow Go fuzz targets cover envelopes, contracts, reducers, lifecycle graphs, privacy, outbox, MCP, pooled reset and canary assignment.

- Every fuzz failure is minimized, root-cause deduplicated and converted into a permanent regression test.

- Production endpoint blocklists and cleanup registry are tested before real-service suites run.

title: Prove RDS Proxy and direct PostgreSQL listener topology
description:
Build an executable oracle for Aurora PostgreSQL outbox wakeups across the launch listener topology: app traffic may use RDS Proxy/pooling, but durable outbox authority remains PostgreSQL and LISTEN/NOTIFY is only a wakeup hint.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- A test harness runs one durable polling consumer plus the chosen listener path through Aurora writer failover and RDS Proxy interruption; every committed outbox row at or below the final watermark is applied exactly once or explicitly deduplicated by revision.
- The harness proves a direct listener reconnect gap cannot lose correctness because cursor polling catches all missed rows.
- The harness proves notifications delivered through an unsupported transaction-pooled path are not required for correctness and cannot be the only delivery mechanism.
- Duplicate, reordered, and missing notifications advance no local snapshot past the durable cursor and do not revive stale policy.
- Metrics expose listener reconnect count, poll catch-up lag, last applied revision, and stale-closed duration.

title: Prove 100-pod bootstrap backpressure and notification storms
description:
Build the horizontal-scaling acceptance oracle that goes beyond the three-pod conformance suite: 100 stateless pods cold-start, catch up from Aurora/PostgreSQL authority, and survive notification storms without making Redis mandatory.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- A 100-pod test boots from empty local state against a bounded Aurora/outbox backlog; pods do not accept protected requests until an initial signed snapshot and required cursors are installed.
- Notification storms, reordered wakeups, and dropped wakeups cannot create duplicate application, cursor regression, stale policy revival, or DB thundering herd beyond configured backpressure limits.
- Backpressure protects Aurora by bounding concurrent bootstrap readers, LISTEN reconnects, snapshot downloads, and per-tenant catch-up work while preserving starvation-free progress.
- Pod, node, and zone loss during bootstrap/recovery leaves surviving pods available within the documented stale-closed rules and lets replacement pods converge from durable state.
- The report records actual lag, queue depth, retry, WAL/autovacuum, and CPU/memory data without inventing benchmark thresholds before measurement.

title: Serialize empty-database model catalog bootstrap across pods
description: Observed during public OCI Helm 2.1.33 replacement proof on a fresh PostgreSQL database: starting replicaCount=3 caused every gateway pod to remain in initializing model catalog while competing for first-seed distributed locks. Scaling gateway to 0, then 1 until ready, then 3 succeeded. Make fresh multi-pod install converge without operator serialization. Acceptance: exact public chart/image starts from empty Postgres at 3 replicas within bounded time; only one pod performs each initial pricing/parameter/MCP seed; contenders wait or load committed rows; lock acquisition and sync have bounded contexts and actionable logs; three pods become Ready on distinct nodes; restart and upgrade retain availability; regression runs in local k3d and CI without public catalog network dependency.
close_reason: Invalidated by clean reproducer. In fresh namespace fg-bootstrap-repro with offline catalog mounted before startup, exact public chart 2.1.33 launched replicaCount=3 concurrently on three distinct nodes and Helm completed revision 1 in under one minute. Initial restarts were PostgreSQL connection-refused before bundled DB readiness; all three recovered automatically. Earlier catalog stall was contaminated by deliberate missing-file crashes and their unexpired 30-second distributed-lock leases, so it did not prove clean-start catalog contention.

title: Gate gateway startup on bundled PostgreSQL readiness
description: Clean public-chart install in fg-bootstrap-repro ultimately succeeded with 3/3 pods across three nodes, but every gateway container restarted twice because it raced the bundled PostgreSQL Service and received connection refused. Make chart startup ordering calm and observable without coupling production deployments to bundled Postgres. Acceptance: when postgresql.enabled=true, an initContainer or equivalent bounded readiness gate waits for DNS/TCP/database readiness before launching the gateway; when using external/Aurora Postgres, behavior remains configurable and startup failures remain bounded/actionable; a clean three-replica k3d install reaches Ready without gateway restarts; Helm timeout and failure semantics remain correct.
close_reason: Implemented in f36e5e44a. Bundled-PostgreSQL-only bounded pg_isready init gate is rendered in Deployment and StatefulSet; external/Aurora path omits it. Template suite passes 41/41. Fresh fg-startup-gate k3d install reached 3/3 Ready on three distinct nodes with INIT_EXIT=0 and gateway RESTARTS=0.

title: Make Helm replacement oracle capacity-safe and wait for full rollout
description: Public v0.3.2-to-v0.3.3 proof reproduced two rollout hazards: required one-pod-per-node anti-affinity with replicaCount equal to node count deadlocks when maxSurge=1/maxUnavailable=0; and helm upgrade --wait returned while one old ReplicaSet pod still served. Acceptance: document and validate compatible strategy/capacity combinations; exact-capacity 3-node proof uses maxSurge=0/maxUnavailable=1 or provisions surge capacity; CI requires kubectl rollout status plus exactly three Ready updated pods, zero old image pods, three distinct nodes, and exact image digest before success; rollback and re-upgrade use the same checks; retained VK is checked from every pod cache.

title: Generate deterministic dependency evidence and canonical SPDX
description: Implement a pinned provenance toolchain with separate networked hydrate and offline generate/verify phases. Discover every distributed Go/npm/Cargo manifest via explicit scopes; hydrate exact module/package sources by go.sum or npm integrity; retain content-addressed license evidence; generate sorted inventory and canonical SPDX 2.3 with source digests. Pin Go/Node/npm/ScanCode/Syft versions and checksums. Acceptance: two clean egress-denied generations are byte-identical; unresolved, conflicting, metadata-only, tool-drift, and unclassified-manifest cases fail closed.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: 2026-07-16 deterministic npm generator slice implemented under scripts/provenancegen. Stdlib-only, no-network CLI derives exact package-lock v3 root+non-link closure with collision detection; requires explicit per-name/version concluded-license evidence; trusted GenerateFiles opens evidence under a bounded root, rejects traversal/escaping symlinks/non-regular/missing/tampered files, and verifies SHA256. Dependencies require valid sha512 SRI and emit real SHA512 package checksums; root emits exact package.json SHA256. Outputs sorted inventory and stable SPDX 2.3 with PURLs, root documentDescribes, DEPENDS_ON relationships, distinct declared/concluded licenses, and caller-supplied timestamp. title: Implement atomic cross-replica hard budget reservations
description: Governance budgets/rate limits are pod-local sync.Map counters periodically dumped to Postgres. Add authoritative atomic reservation/settlement semantics so concurrent replicas cannot overspend hard limits; preserve bounded latency and controlled overdraft policy.
design: Use Aurora/Postgres as authority: add a reservations table keyed by logical_request_id + attempt_id + epoch with unique idempotency constraints, lease expiry, reserved/settled/refunded amounts, and controlled-overdraft metadata. Implement Reserve/Settle/Refund in one transaction with row/advisory locking; wire admission quota stage before provider effect and settlement after response. LISTEN/NOTIFY is only a wake hint; DB rows remain source of truth. Redis is optional acceleration, never mandatory.

title: Design privacy-safe user activity analytics and optimization feedback
description: Design governed user activity analytics and optimization feedback for how internal users operate through Frankengate. Preserve full-fidelity user/team/admin trace access in the source authority while deriving bounded activity events and aggregates asynchronously; credentials are excluded and non-equivalent destinations receive transformed copies. Cover project provenance, skill/tool/MCP usage, domains/data sources, session lifecycle, compaction, latency/cost/retries and opt-in suggestions. Prohibit employee performance ranking and unrelated protected/emotional inference; preserve purpose, region, retention, deletion, consent and cohort policy without degrading individual recall.

title: Define bounded activity and attribution event contract
description: Define versioned compact activity/attribution event schemas for principal pseudonym, virtual-key ID, session/device/client IDs, governed project/workspace class, skill/tool/MCP identifiers, provider/model route, domain/data-source class, timestamps, duration buckets, retries, compaction/context indicators, and outcome. Events stay bounded and content-free but may carry an authorized_source_ref to the full-fidelity trace authority plus content disposition, classification, purpose and policy/authorization/deletion epochs. Separate personal views from aggregate analytics; never treat the compact event as the trace-content authority.

title: Implement privacy-preserving aggregation and access controls
description: Design aggregate query/materialization contracts with minimum cohorts, cell suppression, differential query budgets where needed, complementary-cell/repeated-query resistance, role/purpose checks, deletion propagation and audit. Individual owners and authorized team/admin readers may drill through to governed full-fidelity source rows within their scope; released cross-user aggregates remain minimized and never expose credentials or small cohorts. No manager ranking, employment decisions, or inferred protected/emotional traits.

title: Instrument nearline activity analytics without hot-path coupling
description: Implement an asynchronous bounded PostgreSQL outbox/job path from governed EvidenceEnvelope receipts and authorized source references to activity aggregates and optional Frankensearch indexes. Same-scope workers may resolve full-fidelity content under RLS, purpose, classification, policy/authorization/deletion epochs; credentials are always excluded and an index outside the equivalent governed scope receives a transformed copy. Use separate analytics deployments, queues, pools, budgets and autoscaling from inference, with backpressure, loss accounting, idempotency, schema/index evolution and deletion closure.
acceptance_criteria: Analytics workers claim jobs with bounded leases/idempotency and can stop/restart without loss or duplicate publication. Queue depth/age, processing latency, failure/retry/dead-letter, tenant quota and index watermark metrics drive worker HPA. Saturation, poison jobs, reindex and report bursts cannot exhaust gateway connections, CPU, memory or pod slots; inference SLO comparison is recorded.

title: Build governed optimization suggestions and evaluation loop
description: Define aggregate-only recommendations such as skill/tool substitutions, context or compaction settings, routing/provider changes, caching opportunities, and data-source/MCP reliability improvements. Suggestions must include evidence window, cohort/sample size, uncertainty, privacy receipt, explanation, human approval state, and rollback/expiry. Add offline replay/golden tests and reject suggestions based on sparse, biased, or privacy-ineligible data.

title: Build fast exact-SHA beta artifact lane
description: Create .github/workflows/frankengate-beta.yml for rapid internal binaries. Trigger only on dev path changes or explicit workflow_dispatch with an immutable ref. Resolve and record source SHA; run focused Go compile/vet/race and provenance checks, build UI once, build only Linux amd64 binary without -a, package LICENSE/NOTICE/SPDX/checksum/metadata, and upload a beta-* Actions artifact. No GitHub Release, GHCR, Helm, macOS matrix, or vulnerability scan. Hard budgets: checks 15m, UI 12m, binary 12m; exact artifact names and source/UI hashes; 30s heartbeats and timing summary. Acceptance: push to dev creates one beta run; version tags do not; artifact executes and reports the source SHA; no official publication permissions.

description: Document the Okta application setup required for the FrankenGate dashboard: redirect/logout URIs, issuer and audience configuration, PKCE requirements, required claims, group-to-role mapping, team scoping, cookie/proxy considerations, local development mode, and incident recovery for signing-key or group changes. Add a deterministic operator verification checklist and configuration validation/doctor output that detects missing or unsafe settings before production startup. Acceptance: docs match the actual config schema and routes; examples contain no real secrets; a smoke test validates the configured discovery endpoint and claim mapping without logging credentials.

title: Polish one-click Okta dashboard login and session bootstrap
description: Provide the low-friction dashboard entry path for internal users: unauthenticated users are redirected to the configured Okta issuer with a preserved, validated deep link; returning users bootstrap a server-backed session and land on their authorized team/user dashboard. Support an optional IdP-initiated path only when state/nonce and redirect allowlists remain enforceable. Show actionable loading, denial, expired-session, and unauthorized states; never offer password collection or browser-stored tokens. Acceptance: Playwright proves direct dashboard navigation, deep-link round trip, repeated-login session reuse, logout then re-login, IdP denial, invalid redirect rejection, keyboard/mobile usability, and no token/secret exposure in browser storage, URL fragments, UI, or logs.

title: Add pluggable overdraft alert delivery adapters
description: Implement a durable, idempotent alert fanout boundary for controlled overdraft events. Support an internal event contract with user/team/operator recipients, warning/breach/approval/consumption/expiry event types, deduplication key, severity, policy context, and redacted evidence. Provide adapters for SNS topic publish and generic signed webhook; keep email/in-product as separate consumers. Configuration must make channel choice explicit, fail closed for missing destinations, bound retries/backoff, expose delivery outcome and lag metrics, and never block the inference hot path. Add contract tests for duplicate delivery, retry exhaustion, tenant scoping, PII/token redaction, and disabled-channel behavior. Document that SNS is optional and that approval/alert policy remains authoritative in the durable store.

title: Make 1M-context beta-header routing explicit across Bedrock providers
description: Audit and implement end-to-end 1M-context handling for Anthropic-format requests through Bedrock and Bedrock Mantle, including Claude-visible aliases that convert to OpenAI/Mantle. AWS Bedrock native Messages expects anthropic_beta in the JSON body (the API docs list anthropic_beta, not only an HTTP header); Anthropic-compatible proxy surfaces use anthropic-beta. Verify exact placement per provider surface, provider/model allowlists, overrides, streaming/unary parity, preservation through integration/native Mantle conversion, fail-closed unsupported models, mock transport tests, and capability metadata. Do not infer support solely from a token budget. Pay special attention to OpenAI-compatible Mantle /openai/v1 paths: an Anthropic beta header is not automatically a valid OpenAI request field, so either document the capability as unavailable there or implement an explicit provider translation backed by Mantle documentation.

comments.text: 2026-07-17 research baseline: anthropic.Context1MBetaHeader is context-1m-2025-08-07; ProviderFeatures marks Context1M=true for Anthropic, Vertex, Bedrock, BedrockMantle, Azure. title: Build parameterized 100-pod VK bootstrap and backpressure oracle
description: Add a separate disposable Kubernetes stress harness, not a three-pod substitution. Parameterize replica count (default 100), assert every pod reaches readiness fence, exercise concurrent shared-key bootstrap/rotation/revocation, bound PostgreSQL listener/outbox wakeups and connection usage, inject notification storms, and record admission latency/errors/resource ceilings. Prove stale-closed authority during database partition and recovery. Keep node-placement assumptions explicit for local clusters.

Authenticate with existing OIDC/session or short-lived device/PKCE authorization; issue audience-bound least-privilege scopes for own-trace read, report submit/status/cancel, evidence export/delete, and optional team aggregates. Persist report jobs/results/receipts in PostgreSQL, execute on analytics workers, and use FrankenSearch only as a derived authorized retrieval engine. Never give clients database, index, provider-key or internal service credentials.
acceptance_criteria: A user can authorize a CLI, submit personal trace/usage/skill-gap reports, poll or stream status, inspect citations/coverage/missingness, export/delete eligible evidence and revoke access. Dashboard uses the same API. IDOR, cross-tenant, stale membership, revoked token, replay, scope upgrade, result-cache, cancellation and deletion tests fail closed. Large reports return 202/job IDs, enforce quotas/timeouts, and never execute on inference request workers.

title: Isolate inference, analytics API, and analytics worker scaling classes

Give each independent queues, PostgreSQL pools/roles, resource requests/limits, scaling signals, disruption/placement policy, admission quotas and network policy. Analytics work is asynchronous and cannot run in gateway workers or consume reserved inference capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Rendered Helm exposes independently scalable components and secure defaults, with analytics/FrankenSearch disabled by default. Gateway HPA uses inference concurrency/queue/latency; analytics API uses request/concurrency; workers use eligible queue depth/age and processing time; FrankenSearch uses query concurrency/latency plus resource saturation. Load tests combine peak inference with re-embedding, index rebuild and report bursts and prove inference SLO/budget, database connection reservations, backpressure, cancellation, scale-to-zero/idle where supported, drain and recovery.

title: Classify Franken adoption mode and preserve upstream licensing/provenance
description: For every proposed Franken/Dicklesworthstone component, classify the actual actor and adoption mode: external upstream binary/image/service, linked crate, or vendored/modified derivative. Pin the exact stable tag/commit and transitive closure; record license/rider, notices, artifacts, protocols, redistribution surface and clean-build evidence. Brandon independent use is not treated as OpenAI use merely because an OpenAI model assisted development. Prefer external orchestration so upstream remains independently licensed and upgradeable; linked or modified distributions require explicit combined-work review and attribution.
acceptance_criteria: Each proposed component has a record containing tag/commit, digest, adoption mode, direct/transitive licenses, notices, generated/model artifacts, distribution surface, clean-build result and disposition. CI rejects unknown or unapproved closure for FrankenGate-built artifacts. Helm pins external releases by version/digest and preserves upstream license/attribution. Negative fixtures prove that linked/vendored artifacts cannot conceal rider or transitive obligations behind a permissive wrapper.

title: Add governed A2A agent discovery and delegation boundary
description: Implement optional A2A v1.x compatibility as a separately scalable broker sharing FrankenGate signed catalog, tenant/purpose authorization, credential broker, audit, privacy, budget, health and kill-switch contracts. Keep MCP tools, A2A remote-agent capabilities and installable procedural skills as distinct typed entities. Start with operator-approved Agent Card ingestion and outbound delegation; no public autonomous routing, automatic installation/promotion or inference-hot-path task supervision.
acceptance_criteria: Pin A2A v1.x and implement only declared bindings. Catalog kinds distinguish MCP_SERVER/MCP_TOOL, A2A_AGENT/A2A_CAPABILITY and PROCEDURAL_SKILL; visible, discoverable, installable, invocable and delegable decisions remain separate. Agent Card fetch/callback paths pass SSRF, redirect, DNS-rebinding, size, signature, publisher/domain, mutation and quarantine tests. Delegation uses audience-bound credentials, idempotent task receipts, cancellation/restart recovery, DLP/artifact controls and tenant/purpose reauthorization. Cross-tenant and injection tests fail before metadata/task/artifact exposure or MCP/skill authority expansion. A2A saturation/outage does not affect inference SLO. Dashboard never labels an A2A capability claim as an installable procedural skill.
notes: Architecture decision: docs/roadmap/research/a2a-agent-skill-discovery-fit.md
